subject: ss-medical-oncology
title: Paediatric solid tumours: neuroblastoma, Wilms tumour, retinoblastoma and rhabdomyosarcoma

steps.tx: Sympathetic neural crest lineage malignancies exhibit diverse clinical and biological behaviors. **Neuroblastoma** commonly arises in the adrenal medulla or paraspinal sympathetic ganglia. Genomic amplification of **MYCN** on chromosome 2p occurs in approximately 20% of cases, defining high-risk disease irrespective of age or clinical stage, mandating ultra-intensive multimodal induction, tandem autologous stem cell transplantation, radiation therapy, and anti-GD2 monoclonal antibody immunotherapy.
steps.say: Sympathetic neural crest lineage malignancies exhibit diverse clinical and biological behaviors. Neuroblastoma commonly arises in the adrenal medulla or paraspinal sympathetic ganglia. Genomic amplification of MYCN on chromosome 2p occurs in approximately 20% of cases, defining high-risk disease irrespective of age or stage, mandating intensive chemotherapy, autologous transplant, and anti-GD2 immunotherapy.

left.title: MYCN-Amplified Neuroblastoma
points: Rapid tumour proliferation and early metastasis
High-risk classification across all patient ages
Mandates tandem autologous HSCT and dinutuximab

right.title: Favourable Biological Features
points: Infant age (<18 months) at initial diagnosis

steps.tx: Infants with metastatic neural crest tumours possess an extraordinary capacity for spontaneous differentiation. Neuroblastoma **stage MS** formerly termed stage 4S occurs in infants younger than 18 months presenting with small localized primary tumours and metastases confined strictly to liver, skin, or minimal bone marrow involvement without cortical bone lesions. These tumours frequently undergo complete **spontaneous regression** or maturation into benign ganglioneuromas, managed primarily with watchful supportive observation.

nodes.label: Metastases Limited to Liver, Skin, Marrow

steps.tx: Embryonal renal neoplasms display classic triphasic histology mimicking developing metanephric blastema. **Wilms tumour** nephroblastoma comprises blastemal, epithelial, and stromal mesenchymal elements. In North American COG protocols, upfront radical nephrectomy guides surgical staging, whereas European SIOP protocols administer **preoperative chemotherapy** with vincristine and dactinomycin to shrink the tumour, induce a fibrous pseudocapsule, and prevent intraoperative capsule rupture and peritoneal spill.

In North American COG protocols, upfront radical nephrectomy guides surgical staging, whereas European SIOP protocols administer preoperative chemotherapy with vincristine and dactinomycin to prevent intraoperative rupture.

left.title: COG Paradigm (North America)
points: Upfront radical nephrectomy with lymph node sampling
Accurate untouched pathological and molecular staging
Loss of heterozygosity at 1p and 16q directs therapy

right.title: SIOP Paradigm (Europe / Global)
points: Shrinks primary tumour and forms firm pseudocapsule

steps.tx: Cellular pleomorphism and abnormal mitotic figures define adverse histological subtypes in nephroblastoma. Diffuse **anaplasia** characterized by markedly enlarged multipolar mitotic figures and hyperchromatic pleomorphic nuclei accounts for only 5% of Wilms tumour cases but drives over 50% of disease recurrences. Driven by underlying somatic **TP53 mutations**, anaplastic nephroblastoma displays intrinsic resistance to standard two-drug actinomycin and vincristine protocols, requiring intensive doxorubicin, cyclophosphamide, and etoposide regimens.
steps.say: Cellular pleomorphism and abnormal mitotic figures define adverse histological subtypes in nephroblastoma. Diffuse anaplasia characterized by markedly enlarged multipolar mitotic figures and hyperchromatic nuclei accounts for 5% of Wilms tumour cases but drives half of recurrences. Driven by underlying somatic TP53 mutations, anaplastic tumours require intensive multi-agent chemotherapy regimens.

rows: Atypical mitoses restricted to single locus

steps.tx: Malignant transformation of developing neuroretinal tissue produces characteristic ocular abnormalities. **Retinoblastoma** typically presents with white pupillary reflex **leukocoria** and strabismus in early childhood. Inherited bilateral retinoblastoma results from germline inactivation of the RB1 tumour suppressor gene on chromosome 13q14. Intra-arterial chemotherapy via direct microcatheter infusion of **melphalan** into the ophthalmic artery achieves high globe preservation rates, avoiding external beam radiation.

steps.tx: Pediatric myogenic soft tissue sarcomas segregate into distinct histological and molecular subtypes. **Rhabdomyosarcoma** is categorized into embryonal and alveolar subtypes. **Embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma** ERMS is the most common variant, characterized by loss of heterozygosity at chromosome 11p15, occurring primarily in orbit and genitourinary sites in young children, displaying superior sensitivity to multi-agent chemotherapy with vincristine, dactinomycin, and cyclophosphamide VAC.

Embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma ERMS is the most common variant, characterized by loss of heterozygosity at chromosome 11p15, occurring in orbit and genitourinary sites in young children, displaying favourable prognosis with VAC chemotherapy.

right.title: Alveolar Rhabdomyosarcoma (ARMS)
points: Unfavourable sites: extremity and trunk musculature
Aggressive course with early bone marrow metastasis

steps.tx: Aggressive rhabdomyosarcoma histologies harbour recurrent pathognomonic gene fusions. **Alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma** is defined by chromosomal translocations **t(2;13)(q35;q14)** or t(1;13)(p36;q14), fusing PAX3 or PAX7 with FOXO1. These chimeric transcription factors potently transactivate myogenic oncogenes, driving rapid metastasis to bone marrow and meninges. Modern risk stratification assigns all fusion-positive rhabdomyosarcomas to high-risk intensive multi-agent therapy regardless of primary anatomical location.
steps.say: Aggressive rhabdomyosarcoma histologies harbour recurrent pathognomonic gene fusions. Alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma is defined by chromosomal translocations t(2;13) or t(1;13), fusing PAX3 or PAX7 with FOXO1. These chimeric transcription factors transactivate myogenic oncogenes, driving rapid metastasis to marrow and meninges. Fusion-positive tumours receive intensive therapy regardless of anatomy.

rows: Unfavourable; high rate of systemic relapse
Slightly superior survival compared to PAX3

steps.tx: Systemic immunotherapy directed against ganglioside antigens eliminates microscopic residual neuroblastoma. **Dinutuximab** is a chimeric human-murine monoclonal antibody targeting **disialoganglioside GD2**, expressed on neuroblastoma cells and peripheral sensory nerve fibres. Added to alternating subcutaneous GM-CSF, intravenous IL-2, and oral isotretinoin maintenance in high-risk neuroblastoma, dinutuximab produced a 20% absolute improvement in 2-year event-free survival, requiring continuous opioid analgesia to suppress intense neuropathic pain.
steps.say: Systemic immunotherapy directed against ganglioside antigens eliminates microscopic residual neuroblastoma. Dinutuximab is a chimeric monoclonal antibody targeting disialoganglioside GD2, expressed on neuroectodermal cells and pain fibres. Added to GM-CSF, IL-2, and isotretinoin maintenance in high-risk neuroblastoma, dinutuximab produced a 20% improvement in event-free survival, requiring opioid analgesia for neuropathic pain.
